newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Li Ka-shing flagship group unveils major reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Li Ka-shing flagship group unveils major reshuffle.

text.p: Hong Kong billionaire Li Ka-shing's flagship business group announced a major corporate restructuring on Monday affecting his China infrastructure firm and Hong Kong electricity utility.

The restructuring consists of two major moves and involves all four of the group's listed companies, parent Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd, its 45 percent-held associate Hutchison Whampoa, Hong Kong Electric Holdings Ltd and the newest member of the group, Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd.
The group said that a purchase of shares of Hongkong Electric on Friday had pushed Hutchison's shareholding in the utility to 35.01 percent, triggering a general offer.
Hutchison plans to transfer its stake of 707.53 million shares in Hongkong Electric to Cheung Kong Infrastructure (CKI).
The stake is valued at HK$18.74 billion, based on Hongkong Electric's closing price of HK$26.50, a slight premium to the share's closing price of HK$25.25 on Friday.
CKI will fund the purchase of the stake in Hongkong Electric by issuing to Hutchison 886.21 million new CKI shares at HK$21.15 per share, the share's closing price on Friday.
In the second part of the restructuring, Cheung Kong will transfer its 70.66 percent shareholding in CKI to Hutchison.
The stake is valued at HK$20.45 billion based on CKI's closing price on Friday.
Hutchison will satisfy the purchase with the issue of 349.50 new shares to Cheung Kong.

In the event that a necessary waiver, to be set out in a forthcoming announcement, was not obtained, Cheung Kong would receive 254.32 million new Hutchison shares and about HK$5.57 billion in cash, the announcement said.
Additional details about the offers and the restructuring would be announced soon, it said.
CKI would enjoy a steady cash flow from Electric into its China development projects, many of which required long investment horizons, one analyst said.
"Hongkong Electric has more management skills...It is a big bonus for Cheung Kong Infrastructure," said Fred Kam, investment analyst at New China Hong Kong Securities.
But other analysts disagreed.
"I think the move will have a negative impact on CKI," said Geoffrey Cheng, Hong Kong and China infrastructure analyst at NAVA SC Securities.
The acquisition of Hongkong Electric, which is facing slower earnings growth than CKI, would reduce CKI's growth, said Cheng.

He said the acquisition of the new shares in CKI by Hutchison would raise its stake in the China play to about 85 percent, requiring Hutchison to place out some of those shares to bring its stake below 75 percent to comply with exchange requirements that at least 25 percent of shares are in public hands, putting pressure on the price.

The benefit to Hutchison would be a boost in 1997 earnings from exceptional gains on the sale of its Hongkong Electric shares. Brokers said the company was believed to have acquired them at around HK$5.00 per share in 1985.

As for Cheung Kong, the acquisition of an additional stake in Hutchison would boost the parent's holding over the 50 percent level, allowing it to consolidate Hutchison's earnings, said Archie Hart of BZW Securities.
Trading in the shares of the four listed companies was suspended on Monday.
